tasks.short: Write and review the technical spec for an HR report

today.trigger: An HR business partner, payroll, learning or finance asks for a new or changed report, or a CAO or payroll change breaks a definition already in use.
steps: Sit with the requester and write the question, the population and the decision the report must support.
Look up field names in AFAS Profit, the nightly extract, Recruitee, Studytube and the staffing-agency portals.
Draft measures, filters, row-level access and the refresh rule in a SharePoint document.
Check the draft on a sample in Excel or Power BI, and keep verzuim to rates and durations.
Walk the spec past the requester, flag works-council consent when the report can observe workers, and file it.
drudgery: Copying AFAS field names from old Word specs into a new one
Rewriting headcount, 90-day and verzuim definitions that already exist on another report
Chasing which column the nightly extract actually contains
today.time_sinks: Most of the time goes to finding the AFAS field the nightly extract really uses, and to rewriting a definition that already exists in another report.

lenses.faster: The field hunt and the boilerplate draft drop out, because the draft is taken from the last accepted spec and the semantic model. The sample check and the definition conversation remain and take about three fifths of today's time, since every drafted column still has to be confirmed on the extract.
lenses.autonomous: A report request, or a CAO or payroll change that breaks a definition, starts it. A draft spec is prepared from the approved definitions and the model, and it is filed for build only after the analyst accepts the population, the measures and the access.
lenses.ambitious: Flex workers and night-shift crews are written into the population rules of the 90-day and verzuim specs, so Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo can see those groups in the figures. Demand would grow if a spec were cheap: site managers would ask for agency and shift cuts they currently leave out.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying AFAS field names between old specs and SharePoint. The person wants more of the argument over who counts as a productive hire at day 90.
lenses.options: Two or three population choices, own staff alone or own staff plus flex, and verzuim with or without the CAO waiting-day rule, produce different numbers for the HR Director and the works council. The draft that is accepted becomes the number the company will use.
lenses.altitude: The week becomes a short list of accepted definitions and sample checks, with the right to block a report that uses a private definition or an access rule the list does not allow. The job becomes more expert, on CAO coverage, AVG limits and what managers will be judged on.
reach: The FP&A analyst's task of specifying the monthly labour-cost and FTE bridge, after learning the AFAS general-ledger mapping and the Controller's close calendar.
The payroll specialist's task of stating which new CAO wage component enters the labour-cost report, after learning AFAS payroll element codes and the Beroepsgoederenvervoer wage table.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst can judge whether a definition is fair under the CAO and acceptable to the works council, and whether a sample that matches the extract is the population managers will be judged on. Plausible AFAS field names still have to be rejected by that person.
tasks.pattern_why: The shape of a spec is predictable, and a model can draft it from the last accepted spec and the semantic model. The analyst stays the lead because the population, the measure and the access become the number the company stands behind.

in_practice.trigger: A requester submits a report change, or a CAO or payroll change invalidates a definition on the approved list.
steps: Pull the approved definitions, the last spec and the semantic-model fields.
Draft the spec: question, population, measures, filters, refresh, row-level security, and a works-council flag when personal or absence data is in scope.
Run the measures on a sample of the nightly AFAS extract and list rows and field names that do not match.
The analyst corrects the definitions and removes any field the extract does not contain.
The analyst walks the spec past the requester and files the accepted version on SharePoint as the build source.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst accepts the spec before anyone builds or publishes the report. A report that can show absence, performance or individual presence is flagged for the works council and does not skip that route.
data_needed: Approved definitions for headcount, 90-day retention and verzuim
The nightly extract's actual column list
Power BI row-level security roles and the minimum group size
CAO population rules for own staff and flex workers
The works-council consent log for people reports
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint spec library, with the accepted definition written back to the metric list and the sample-check result attached.

evidence.claim: Power BI Copilot answers questions on a prepared semantic model, summarises reports and writes DAX, on Fabric F2+ or Premium capacity. Without a prepared model it can misinterpret the data, and non-English chat is not officially supported.
Uber's QueryGPT cut writing a query from about 10 minutes to about 3 minutes, and 78% of early users said it saved time. Hallucinated table and column names remain unsolved.

Works-council consent is required for processing personal data and for a facility that can observe presence, behaviour or performance (WOR art. 27(1)(k) and (l)). Capability is the test, and productivity dashboards almost always qualify.

Absence data is health data under GDPR art. 9. The Dutch data protection authority fined a firm EUR 15,000 partly for recording the cause of sick leave, so verzuim reporting stays with rates and durations.
One consultant's reading of Dutch practice is that totals still count for works-council consent when the tool stores per-user rows.

risks: A drafted spec can name AFAS columns that are not on the nightly extract, and a later build would then use the wrong field. QueryGPT-style column hallucinations are unsolved.
A verzuim definition that stores sickness cause, or a cut small enough to identify a person, conflicts with AVG art. 9. The EUR 15,000 fine was partly for recording that cause.
Power BI Copilot needs Fabric F2+ or Premium, and Dutch chat is outside official support, so a Dutch spec can look finished and still misstate a CAO measure.
A totals report built on per-user rows can still be a WOR art. 27 matter. Filing the spec straight to build can open the one-month nullity window.
research_questions: On the last ten report requests, what share of field names in a model-drafted spec exist as columns on the nightly AFAS extract?
Does this Power BI tenant have Fabric F2+ or Premium capacity, and must the spec be in Dutch?
How many live HR reports still match their SharePoint spec? If the spec is already ignored, a faster draft does not change the numbers.
For which cuts, flex, night shift or agency, would the works council require fresh consent under WOR art. 27?

tasks.short: Scan HR technology trends and brief the HR Director

today.trigger: A renewal or a release of AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube or Power BI is coming up, or the HR Director asks whether a workforce-technology trend is worth using at the three sites.
steps: Collect vendor release notes, Microsoft and AFAS pages, and Dutch sources such as AWVN on the question asked.
List what would change in AFAS Profit, Power BI, Recruitee, Studytube or the agency portals.
Match that to internal users: site managers, recruiters, payroll, the works council and the people who order flex staff.
Write a short note with the choice to adopt, wait or pilot, plus consent and AVG consequences.
Take the vendor call when one is needed and correct the note from what was said.
drudgery: Pasting marketing claims into a slide
Re-typing the same AVG and works-council caveats
Keeping the list of source links
today.time_sinks: Most of the time is reading and summarising. The judgment at the end is short, and a vendor call is rare and long.

lenses.faster: Reading release notes and writing the first brief drop out. Source checks, the recommendation and vendor calls remain and take a little under half of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A renewal date, a product release or a question from the HR Director starts it. The scan drafts a brief with links and caveats from the agreed sources, and the brief is sent only after the analyst approves the recommendation. Vendor conversations stay with the analyst.
lenses.ambitious: A new quarterly note to the works council flags HR-technology changes that could observe presence, behaviour or performance, in time for consent before a pilot. Demand would grow if the note were cheap: the OR and the site managers would ask for one on flex-agency portals and on each proposed pilot, instead of waiting for the annual HR plan.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss pasting vendor claims into slides. The person wants more of the judgment on whether a trend changes day-90 retention or verzuim in the three warehouses.
lenses.options: Three briefs on the same sources, renew, wait for the next release, or pilot on one site after works-council consent, lead to different spend and different data duties. Choosing the brief is the decision the HR Director takes.
lenses.altitude: The week holds a few approved briefs at renewals and releases, plus the vendor calls. The analyst can withhold a claim that has no source and can mark a pilot as requiring works-council consent before it starts. The job becomes more expert on lawful adoption for this CAO workforce.
reach: The learning and development specialist's task of judging a Studytube change for forklift, VCA and food-safety renewals, after learning the mandatory-training matrix and how completions are written back to AFAS.
The compensation and benefits specialist's first look at a tool that administers a CAO wage element or a benefit, after learning the wage structure the payroll specialist already runs.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst can separate a vendor's own claim from a change that would hold on Noordhaven's AFAS extract, the agency portals and the CAO, and can see when a tool needs works-council consent or would touch sickness causes. Calls with vendors and with the works council stay with the person.
tasks.pattern_why: A scan follows a fixed outline: what changed, what it does on Noordhaven's systems, who inside the company would use it, what the source fails to prove, and a recommendation. One model call can turn release notes and articles into that brief, and the analyst approves it before it is sent. Vendor calls sit outside the step.

in_practice.trigger: A renewal date, a named product release, or a question from the HR Director about a tool.
steps: Collect the agreed sources: vendor release notes, Microsoft Learn, AWVN or works-council material, and the last Noordhaven brief.
Draft a two-page brief: what changed, the effect on AFAS, Power BI, Recruitee or Studytube, who is affected, consent and AVG flags, and what the source does not prove.
Attach the links and mark every figure that is a vendor's or a survey's own claim.
The analyst checks the links, drops what does not apply to the three sites and the flex agencies, and writes adopt, wait or pilot.
The analyst sends the approved brief. Any vendor meeting stays on the analyst's calendar.
in_practice.human_gate: No brief leaves without the analyst's approval. A pilot that could observe presence, behaviour or performance is marked for works-council consent and is not written as already decided.
systems: agreed public and vendor source list
data_needed: Renewal dates and live modules for AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and Power BI
The agreed source list and the prior briefs
A description of what the nightly extract and the agency portals do and do not contain
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint trend-brief library, each brief kept with its source links and the analyst's accept or reject note.

evidence.claim: Visier's Vee answers people-analytics questions in Teams or Slack. Its '10x' figure is a vendor line and no customer is named.

Microsoft's Workforce Insights agent shows managers staffing and hiring, and warns that faster access to information does not, by itself, lead to better decisions. No separate customer result is published.
Workday's own HR-team write-up says the hardest part was quantifying value after the agent was built. Workday also says its customer data does not establish how much of a reported decline AI caused.
In a Visier survey, 48% of 1,000 US employees said they had exaggerated their AI use, so adoption surveys run high.

Emotion inference at work is banned, and a chatbot must disclose that it is AI. From 2 December 2027, AI that allocates tasks on behaviour or evaluates performance is high-risk and needs a human overseer, logs and information to workers' representatives.

risks: A brief can carry Visier's unattributed '10x', or a survey in which 48% of people said they exaggerated AI use, into a renewal decision at Noordhaven.
Microsoft's own caveat applies here: a faster brief does not by itself make the adopt-or-wait decision better, and Workday reports that value after the fact was the hard part to show.
A pilot that evaluates performance or allocates work on behaviour becomes high-risk AI on 2 December 2027, and emotion inference of workers is already banned.
Release notes that sit behind a partner login will be missing, and the brief can still look complete.
research_questions: Which renewals, pilots or consent filings did the last four technology briefs actually change?
What share of the figures in those briefs were vendor or survey claims with no result Noordhaven can check?
Will the works council treat a quarterly technology note as input to consent, and how many days before a pilot must it arrive?
Which AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and Microsoft release notes can be read without a sales call?

role.altitude: The analyst's week moves to the metric layer managers and the HR Director query: definitions, access, sample checks and the briefs that sit on them. The analyst gains the right to stop a number or a tool claim that fails the definition list or that needs works-council consent. The job becomes more expert, on what a people number means under the CAO, the AVG and the OR.
reach: The HR business partner's ad hoc pull of site headcount, 90-day retention and verzuim totals, once the semantic model, row-level security and a minimum group size are in place.
The FP&A analyst's specification of the monthly labour-cost and FTE bridge, after learning the AFAS general-ledger mapping and the Controller's close calendar.
The learning and development specialist's check that forklift, VCA and food-safety completions in Studytube match the matrix and the AFAS record.
role.ceiling_note: One analyst at EUR 78 an hour cannot also sign the payroll, sit as the works council, or read a sickness cause. Verzuim stays rates and durations, including where Wet verbetering poortwachter needs dates, and figures stop where the nightly AFAS extract and the three agency portals stop. Individual performance or attrition scores stay out of this role, and from 2 December 2027 a tool that evaluates performance still needs a human overseer.
skills_to_grow: Write and test definitions of 90-day retention and verzuim that stay at group level and match the CAO, including flex workers where the data allows.
Govern a Power BI semantic model with row-level security, a minimum group size and Dutch measure names checked against the extract.
Read AFAS payroll elements and general-ledger links well enough to specify a report for payroll and the Controller.
Apply WOR art. 27, AVG art. 9 and the EU AI Act high-risk duties before any people-analytics pilot.
Check a sourced brief against the primary link and mark vendor and survey claims before the HR Director sees them.
role.ambitious_version: The analyst keeps one metric layer the HR Director, finance and the three site HR business partners can query: the share of open roles filled by someone productive and still here at day 90, and verzuim by site, correct by day two, as totals the works council has consented to. Night shifts and flex workers sit inside those definitions where the agency data is good enough. The analyst's week is the exceptions, the next definition and the consent note, and a routine manager question is answered from that layer.
